title.narrative: Emergency health and NFIs response for earthquake-affected populations in Hama and Idleb Governorates

description.narrative:
Main goal: Contribute to save lives through the provision of timely, targeted, and appropriate health services and NFIs in Syria.
Outcome 1: Improved access to life-saving primary health care (PHC) services for vulnerable individuals affected by the earthquake in Hama and Idleb Governorates.
Outcome 2: Vulnerable individuals have improved their living conditions during extremely harsh weather conditions in areas heavily affected by the earthquake in Hama and Idleb Governorates.

The proposed emergency intervention will be implemented in communities that have been heavily affected by the earthquake in Hama and Idleb Governorates, targeting vulnerable individuals through the provision of life-saving humanitarian assistance.

The response will be implemented across the governorates of Hama and Idleb and will be focused on the locations most affected by the earthquake. Target sub-districts will be defined in coordination with SARC based on ongoing damage mapping and locations of the collective shelters that are set up to host individuals who lost their housing. At the time of writing, rescue teams are still on the ground and buildings and infrastructures’ assessments are ongoing. Reports of families and individuals on the move see displacement within the same governorates and across governorates seeking for relatives’ refuge or collective shelters. Overall, 36,900 individuals (4,208 M, 14,102 W, 9,071 B, 9,521 G) are expected to benefit from this intervention.

activity-date.narrative: Project end date extended from 6 November 2023 to 29 February 2024 through NCE approved by the donor on 2 October 2023.

sector.narrative: NFI (Winter kits, Core NFIs, Dignity Kits and Hygiene Kits)

title.narrative: Output 2.1 - Vulnerable individuals affected by the earthquake in Hama and Idleb are provided with life-saving non-food items
# of individuals provided with relief kits

comment.narrative: Between April and June 2023, INTERSOS continued distributing relief kits to earthquake-affected communities in Hama and Idleb, reaching a total of 5,291 individuals (521 M, 740 W, 1,893 B, 2,137 G). More into details, 1,383 individuals were provided with dignity kits (423 W, 960 G), 2,493 individuals with hygiene kits (318 M, 28 W, 1,544 B, 549 G), 115 individuals with winter kits (cloths) (13 M, 5 W, 41 B, 56 G), and 1,354 individuals with 365 core NFIs kits (190 M, 284 W, 308 B, 572 G). Following authorization from SARC, core NFIs kits were transported from Damascus to SARC’s warehouse in Hama in May 2023 and distributions started in June 2023 (upon needs assessments conducted in earthquake-affected communities in Hama).

Between February (for winter kits and hygiene kits) and March 2023 (for dignity kits), INTERSOS started distributing relief kits to earthquake-affected communities in Hama and Idleb, reaching a total of 2,844 individuals (432 M, 580 W, 876 B, 956 G). More into details, 617 individuals were provided with dignity kits (161 W, 456 G), 500 individuals with hygiene kits (125 M, 361 B, 14 G), and 1,727 individuals with winter kits (cloths) (307 M, 419 W, 515 B, 486 G). The procurement process of the core NFIs started in February 2023 and the purchase order was signed in the first week of April 2023.

Between July and September 2023, INTERSOS continued with distribution of core NFIs kits based on field assessments conducted in partnership with SARC. 219 individuals (53 M, 54 W, 53 B, 59 G) benefitted from the distribution of 55 kits.

No distributions were conducted over the reporting period, while INTERSOS maintained close coordination with SARC to monitor the movement of displaced families to target them with remaining kits. An assessment was conducted in Khan Sheykoun, where the 2 temporary shelters are expected to close. Yet, the transfer of hosted families to pre-fab accommodations is on hold due to pending installation of latrines. In October 2023, INTERSOS launched the procurement process for the additional 340 kits to be distributed to earthquake-affected communities, but its closure was delayed by procurement-related challenges (i.e. insufficient number of suppliers who submitted their offer due to inflation and market volatility).

title.narrative: Output 1.1 - Capacities of the health care system are strengthened to guarantee the continuity of care and provision of PHC services to individuals affected by the earthquake in Hama and Idleb Governorates
# of individuals having access to primary health care consultations

comment.narrative: 2 Mobile Health Units (MHUs) were deployed to Idleb (Khan Sheykun and Ma’arat Al Numan) in May 2023, while 1 Mobile Medical Team (MMT) was activated in Hama and started targeting earthquake-affected locations with high presence of IDPs in June 2023. Overall, 1,151 individuals (25 M, 582 W, 219 B, 325 G) were provided with medical consultations. The deployment of the 2 MHUs to Idleb (Khan Sheykun and Ma’arat Al Numan) and 1 MMT to Hama (EQ-affected areas) was delayed due to internal challenges with the procurement of the vehicles.

Between July and September 2023, INTERSOS and SARC continued operating 2 Mobile Health Units (MHUs) in Idleb (Khan Sheykun and Ma’arat Al Numan) and 1 Mobile Medical Team (MMT) in Hama. Overall, 2,708 individuals (206 M, 1,038 W, 657 B, 807 G) were provided with medical consultations.

Between October and December 2023, INTERSOS and SARC continued operating 2 Mobile Health Units (MHUs) in Idleb (Khan Sheykun and Ma’arat Al Numan) and 1 Mobile Medical Team (MMT) in Hama. Overall, 3,145 individuals (501 M, 1,129 W, 733 B, 782 G) were provided with medical consultations.

title.narrative: Outcome 1 - Improved access to life-saving primary health care (PHC) services for vulnerable individuals affected by the earthquake in Hama and Idleb Governorates
# of individuals reached by health services (including consultations and awareness sessions)

comment.narrative: 2 Mobile Health Units (MHUs) were deployed to Idleb (Khan Sheykun and Ma’arat Al Numan) in May 2023, while 1 Mobile Medical Team (MMT) was activated in Hama and started targeting earthquake-affected locations with high presence of IDPs in June 2023. Overall, 1,151 individuals (25 M, 582 W, 219 B, 325 G) were provided with medical consultations. The deployment of the 2 MHUs to Idleb (Khan Sheykun and Ma’arat Al Numan) and 1 MMT to Hama (EQ-affected areas) was delayed due to internal challenges with the procurement of the vehicles. With regards to the health and hygiene awareness sessions, on 25 and 26 June 2023, INTERSOS, in coordination with SARC, organized a training for 9 CHVs, which covered the following topics: prevention of Leishmania, prevention of Cholera, Menstrual Hygiene Management, Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) in emergencies, and Reproductive Health (RH) key messages. The training of CHVs was requested by SARC as a precondition for their field deployment - which took place after the training in July 2023.

Between July and September 2023, INTERSOS and SARC continued running 2 Mobile Health Units (MHUs) in Idleb (Khan Sheykun and Ma’arat Al Numan) and 1 Mobile Medical Team (MMT) in Hama. In parallel, 9 Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) were deployed alongside the MHUs/MMT to conduct health and hygiene awareness sessions. Overall, 5722 individuals were reached, including 2,708 individuals (206 M, 1,038 W, 657 B, 807 G) provided with medical consultations and 3,014 individuals (767 M, 1,121 W, 530 B, 596 G) with health and hygiene awareness.

Between October and December 2023, INTERSOS and SARC continued running 2 Mobile Health Units (MHUs) in Idleb (Khan Sheykun and Ma’arat Al Numan) and 1 Mobile Medical Team (MMT) in Hama. In parallel, 9 Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) were deployed alongside the MHUs/MMT to conduct health and hygiene awareness sessions. Overall, 15,985 individuals were reached, including 3,145 individuals (501 M, 1,129 W, 733 B, 782 G) provided with medical consultations and 12,840 individuals (3,671 M, 4,386 W, 2,142 B, 2,641 G) with health and hygiene awareness.
